news.title: Wolves host documentary of World Cup fans who did not return
news.lede: A screening of a documentary about a group of Wolves fans who went to the 1986 World Cup in Mexico and did not return to the Black Country will take place at the club. The group decided not to return to their Stourbridge and Lye homes after attending the global football spectacular, embarking on new lives in the US instead. Gary Allen, who settled in Atlanta and who pitched the documentary, said "Wolves called us and said 'would you like to do the first screening in the UK at the Molineux? And of course all being Wolves fans we said 'we'd love to'."

news.title: Ghana amputee national team facing Türkiye Friday night at Football World Cup in Mexico
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge are chasing a place in the final of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico when they face defending champions Türkiye on Friday night [Nov 20]. Five matches into the tournament, the players are yet to receive their allowances from the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, according to National Paralympic Committee (NPC) Ghana President Samson Deen. This is despite the Ghana Football Association (GFA) activating a US$500,000 sponsorship allocation from Gold Fields Ghana for amputee football. Deen said the national team had not received its financial entitlements despite its performances at the tournament.

news.title: Bozza’s warning as coach weighs up big Socceroos decision
news.lede: Mark Bosnich has called for Football Australia to “roll the contract over” and keep Tony Popovic in charge of the Socceroos for at least another 12 months. It is unclear if Popovic has led the nation for the final time as a manager, with his contract set to expire in late January when the Asian Cup was originally scheduled. Popovic took the Socceroos to the round of 32 at the World Cup. Due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, the tournament was postponed to December 2027 and Popovic has yet to ink a deal to remain in charge until then.

news.title: Uli Hoeneß takes jab at Julian Nagelsmann’s handling of World Cup
news.lede: Uli Hoeneß is already making it pretty clear what he expects from Jürgen Klopp’s Germany tenure, and there might be a little side-eye directed toward the previous regime in the process. Hoeneß believes Klopp will bring discipline, hunger, and a renewed sense of urgency to the national team, while taking a subtle shot at Julian Nagelsmann’s approach to team culture, particularly the infamous family-oriented World Cup camp. ”I don’t think there will be another family outing with player wives and children under Jürgen. I believe he will bring discipline and hunger back.
